replies.body:
Yes. 

The script, in its current state, expects the packages inside `graphql-java-common-12.0` module to be of the format `.../graphql/java/common/v12_0/...`, but the packages are actually named `.../graphql/common/v12_0/...`. 

It only removes `-java` when it appears right before the version number at the end of the module name. If `java` appears anywhere else in the name (which it does in the case of this module), the script does not remove it. Because of that, it still expects the full `...graphql/java/common/v12_0/...` sequence in the package path.

We could fix this generically by stripping `-java-` when it appears as a middle segment (after removing the version), instead of only stripping `-java` at the end. That would handle `graphql-java-common` correctly while still preserving modules like `java-http-client`, where java is the first segment.

Please let me know the approach you’d like me to take.
